mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between an Incline Conveyor and an Elevator?

acceptedAnswer.text: An incline conveyor carries cases continuously along a sloped path and needs enough horizontal distance to gain height. An elevator lifts cases in a compact vertical footprint and suits plants where floor space is the constraint. TRF selects between them during layout engineering, based on the unit, the height, the footprint and the rate of the line.

A lowerator is the module that brings cases down to a lower level in a compact vertical footprint, the counterpart of an elevator. It is typically used when cases leave a packing area on a raised platform or mezzanine and must reach floor level. In TRFIntraflow, it is paired with accumulation and metering so the flow stays paced after the level change.

mainEntity.name: Can Elevation Conveyors Keep Barcode or Vision Data Attached to Each Case?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, where the project requires it. TRFIntraflow includes barcode and vision interfaces, and the controls keep the identification of each case as it moves through the modules, including a level change. That allows sorting, rejecting and routing decisions to be made after the elevation module, with the data each case must carry defined during project engineering.

Manufacturers that run packaging and end-of-line processes on more than one level, or in plants where floor space is limited. TRFIntraflow serves mid-sized and large manufacturers in food processing, beverage, CPG, protein, frozen food, pet food, personal care and industrial sectors.
